en.name: MyFinance
en.short_description: Private offline ledger for spending, budgets and subscriptions. No bank login.
en.subtitle: Offline budget and ledger
en.promotional_text: A first run is empty, because every figure comes from what you enter. No bank connection, no account, and nothing leaves your phone.
en.description:
MyFinance is a private ledger for money you enter yourself, kept in a database on your phone.

A FIRST RUN IS EMPTY
There is no demo balance waiting for you. The app opens with nothing in it, and every figure you see afterwards is calculated from rows you added. If you would rather look around first, More options has Load sample data, which adds a clearly marked, made-up ledger that you can remove again in one tap without touching anything you entered yourself.

TRANSACTIONS
Record income and spending with a description, an amount, a category, a date and an optional note. Tap any row to edit or delete it. The home screen totals income, expenses and the net for the current month, and your balance is the sum of your opening balance and every transaction on file.

BUDGETS
Set a monthly limit for a category. Each budget shows what you have spent against it so far this month with a progress bar, and marks the ones you have gone over.

SUBSCRIPTIONS
Record recurring charges as weekly, monthly or yearly. MyFinance converts them to a common monthly figure so the total is comparable, and rolls each next charge date forward as it passes. The home screen lists what is due in the next thirty days.

EXPORT
Your transactions can be written to a CSV file and handed to the share sheet, so the data stays yours.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
MyFinance does not connect to a bank. There is no sync, no import and no account, nothing is uploaded, and the app works with no network connection at all. It also has no passcode or biometric lock, so anyone who can unlock your phone can open your ledger. There are no ads and nothing to buy. The interface is in English.

review_information.notes:
No account, no sign-in, no permission prompts and no network calls. MyFinance can be reviewed in airplane mode.

Everything visible on first launch is demo data bundled in the binary: the 18,432.75 headline balance, ten transactions such as "Salary Deposit" and "Whole Foods Market", six subscriptions and the monthly budget list are constants. There is no bank connection, sync or import in this version, so nothing on screen is waiting on a server or failing to load.

The interactive part is the add button, which opens "Add Transaction": type a description and an amount, using a negative number for spending, and it is inserted at the top of the Transactions list while the income and expense totals recalculate (the headline balance is a fixed demo figure and does not move). Transactions added this way are held in memory for the session only and are gone after a relaunch, because this build has no storage layer.

The four tabs are Home, Transactions, Budgets and Subscriptions, and all four work with no setup. No ads, no in-app purchase, and no account deletion flow because there is no account.

Transactions, subscriptions and budgets are all constants. pubspec has no http, no bank aggregator, and no local database — there is nowhere for a real transaction to come from or be saved to.
